### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A21 each occurred in about 30-36 in 100 traces, were mostly alternatives to one another, and about 97-99 in 100 of their observed successors were A29; in the later window, each occurred in only about 1 in 200 traces, and pairs of them were absent from about 99 in 100 traces. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL007, REL008, REL016, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- In the earlier window, A26 and A27 were not observed and A28 was observed in only about 1 in 200 traces; in the later window, A26, A27 and A28 each occurred in about 100 in 100 traces and co-occurred with one another in about 100 in 100 traces. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL031, REL032, REL037]
- The later A26/A27/A28 group has no fixed internal order: for each pair, about half of the traces show one order and about half the reverse, and the three activities precede A29 in about 99 in 100 traces. [REL031, REL032, REL037, REL033, REL038, REL042]
- A29 remains in about 100 in 100 traces in both windows, but its relation to the old alternatives changes: earlier, A19/A20/A21 preceded A29 in the traces where they occurred; later, A29 is present without them in about 99 in 100 traces. [POS008, REL012, REL020, REL027]
- A44's observed successors shift from A19/A20/A21 and A10 in the earlier window to A26/A27/A28 in the later window: earlier, about 23-27 in 100 of A44's outgoing transitions went to each of A19/A20/A21 and about 23 in 100 to A10; later, about 30-33 in 100 went to each of A26/A27/A28 and only about 2-3 in 100 to A10. [DIR009]
- A44 precedes the new group in about 99-100 in 100 traces in the later window, and the lag from A44 to A29 increases from mostly 2-3 steps to mostly 4-5 steps, while A29's mean event position shifts from about 0.40 to about 0.44. [REL034, REL039, REL043, LAG005, POS008]
- A10 is less frequent in the later window, from about 26 in 100 traces to about 11 in 100 traces, and its co-occurrence with A19/A20/A21 disappears: earlier it co-occurred with them in about 6-11 in 100 traces, later it is absent from about 89 in 100 traces in which the new group is present. [OCC001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

- The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, a new nearly mandatory unordered segment A26, A27, A28 is inserted after A44 and before A29, while the earlier alternative activities A19, A20, A21 before A29 become almost absent. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR009, REL007, REL008, REL016, REL031, REL032, REL037, REL033, REL038, REL042, REL034, REL039, REL043, REL012, REL020, REL027, LAG005]
- The signs are direct and consistent: A26/A27/A28 go from absent or rare to present in all observed traces and co-occur with one another without fixed order; A19/A20/A21 go from common alternatives to almost absent; A44's successors shift to the new group, A44 precedes it, and the A44-to-A29 lag increases; A29 remains present and follows the new group. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR009, REL007, REL008, REL016, REL031, REL032, REL037, REL034, REL039, REL043, LAG005, POS008, REL033, REL038, REL042]
- The evidence contains 74 control-flow items against an expected 0.82 without change, and no time or resource items, so the pattern is not what an unchanged process typically produces and timing/resource allocation are not assessed. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038, REL039, REL040, REL041, REL042, REL043, REL044, REL045, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]
- Limitations: the later occurrences of A19/A20/A21 are based on one trace each, so their exact later successors are weak. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Other differences: A10 becomes less frequent, loses co-occurrence with A19/A20/A21, and its observed successors shift away from A19/A20/A21 toward A27, A26 and other activities; this may be part of the same re-routing or a separate change. [OCC001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001]
- A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the later window contains a different case mix or a new variant that makes the old alternatives rare, rather than a confirmed structural replacement. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL031, REL032, REL037]
